title: Implement press-resilience and theme-coalescing for floating action buttons
creator: Asha Patel
description: Refactor the floating action / icon-only button surface to use a small set of new, token-driven press-state properties and introduce a cancelable-loading affordance for long-running actions. Goal: reduce flicker/regression across themes, improve press resilience when users abort gestures, and centralize theme coalescing so variants behave consistently across light, dark, and high-contrast modes.
background: We have recurring regressions where floating icon buttons shift size or lose contrast when a loading spinner is shown. Mobile teams reported that long-press cancellation and accidental double-taps are resulting in ambiguous visual feedback. Current styles are duplicated across components and don't expose a simple press/cancel contract to the runtime. This ticket consolidates tokens and prescribes behavior (press, cancel, deferred-loading, motion-reduced) specifically for floating/icon-only buttons.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce three tokens: --btn-press-opacity, --btn-press-elevation-offset, --btn-cancel-threshold (defaults and theme overrides) and document them in the tokens page
Floating/icon-only buttons use token values and render no layout-shift when entering a cancelable-loading state
Press state persists until either a successful action resolution or an explicit cancel gesture within cancel-threshold; accidental taps must show a reversible micro-state
High-contrast and dark themes pass color-contrast checks for pressed and loading states (WCAG AA)
Design system stories (Chromatic) for: default, pressed, long-press-start, canceled, loading->success, loading->error
Unit/regression visual tests added and passing in CI; a short playbook describing how to triage related regressions is attached
Implementation docs and migration notes for engineering outlining token fallback rules and runtime expectations
tasks: Draft token spec and fallback strategy
Update Figma components and export updated tokens
Add CSS variables and documentation in DS site
Implement cancelable-loading overlay pattern in component library
Add unit and visual regression tests
Coordinate with mobile design lead for parity notes
Write rollout plan and backwards-compatible flags
decisions_and_tradeoffs: We choose token expansion (3 tokens) instead of separate variants per theme to limit combinatorial complexity; increases runtime responsibility to coalesce tokens
Cancelable-loading uses a non-blocking micro-spinner anchored inside the button rather than replacing label so there is zero layout shift; tradeoff: slightly more complex CSS positioning
Motion reduction: when user-level reduced-motion is on, the pressed elevation becomes a subtle opacity change only to maintain accessibility
We will default --btn-cancel-threshold to 350ms but allow customers to override in Dedicated/Private via runtime config

notes: Tie telemetry event 'button.cancel' and 'button.loading' to an observability dashboard so we can catch regressions in customer flows. There's an outstanding conversation about whether the micro-spinner should be considered part of token surface or an implementation detail; decided to keep it implementation-scoped but documented.
